content.comment_body: Hello everyone, The manual for the [product_name] KNX communication module mentions support for up to 50 communication objects. Does this mean it can handle 50 separate communication devices, such as connecting 50 KNX thermostats to one [product_name]? Also, how many KNX modules can be used with a single [product_name]? Thank you

Hi, Are you familiar with KNX systems? You can transmit up to 50 pieces of digital or analog information between the [product_name] and the KNX module. Each of these 50 data points can be sent to multiple KNX devices, or the [product_name] can receive 50 data points from KNX devices. The manual states that only one KNX module can be installed per [product_name]. Hope this is helpful.

Hello [user_name], Thank you for your response; I am new to KNX and this is my first time working with it. Could I ask another question for clarification? Does this mean I can connect 50 KNX devices to a single KNX module, or is it one KNX module that transmits 50 different tags or signals? Thank you for your patience.

Hi, That’s not correct—KNX works differently. For example, in [product_name], a digital signal used as an alarm is just one datapoint in the KNX module. On the KNX side, this alarm can be displayed by any connected device. To better grasp the KNX system, attending a KNX workshop could help you understand the key differences from factory automation. These differences are crucial, and without this knowledge, it may be challenging to use the [product_name] KNX module effectively. Hope this clarifies things.
A new question posted by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread, with the subject: Commissioning of the [product_name] EIB/KNX module [article_no] using ETS5. Best regards, [user_name]
